text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: auth/token-validate error rate spike detected — 401s and 5xx on /v1/auth/validate (us-west-2, eu-central-1)

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Triggered for service `auth-service` (PD-Key: PD12345). Escalation policy: oncall-auth -> sre-team.

ashley.k: acked. I'm on call. starting triage, grabbing traces and recent deploys.

devon: +1 saw spikes in the dashboards. High request volume from clients on dedicated infra too. Any deploys in last 30m?

mike: rolled out small signing-key refresh 10m ago to canary (auth-signing v1.3.2) but rollout was supposed to be gradual. I'll check rollout state.

ashley.k: checking key rotation logs now. `kubectl logs -n auth auth-signing-0` shows `failed to load jwks: kid mismatch` repeatedly.

ashley.k: hypothesis: canary started shipping tokens signed with new `kid` before JWKS propagated to validators -> validators returning 401.

support-bot: Customer impact: several API clients reporting `401 invalid_signature` and token validation latency increased. Affected: hosted API, limited dedicated clusters in us-west and eu-central. No data plane writes affected.

mike: rolling back signing service to v1.3.1 on canary now. `kubectl set image deployment/auth-signing auth-signing=redwood/auth-signing:v1.3.1 --record`

ashley.k: while rollback proceeds, can we force JWKS refresh on validators? devon can you push a cache flush?

devon: flushing JWKS cache across validators. running:
```
curl -X POST https://auth-internal.example.com/admin/refresh-jwks -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
I'll iterate across regions.

ashley.k: :white_check_mark: rollback started, validators cache flush in progress. monitoring auth-validate 5m window.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Acknowledgement recorded (ashley.k). If issue not resolved in 15m, escalation to SRE lead.

sara: heads-up: support queue getting ticket flood, adding a canned response to explain token error + recommended client retry. tagging affected customers for manual reachout.

ashley.k: auth-validate 401 rate down from 28% -> 3% after cache flush/rollback. Latency back to baseline. still watching for stragglers.

mike: found the deploy script didn't set `jwks_propagation=grace_period` flag. will open PR to gate canary key rotations behind cache-propagation hook.

devon: running smoke tests: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <sample-token>" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/auth/validate` before -> `HTTP/1.1 401` ; after -> `HTTP/1.1 200` (body: `{ "valid": true, "kid": "old-kid" }`).

ashley.k: next steps: 1) revert accidental canary (done), 2) add jwks propagation check in rollout pipeline, 3) schedule emergency key-rotation postmortem and communicate to customers with dedicated infra about upcoming forced rotate windows.

mike: PR opened: `github.com/redwood/auth/PR#489` adds waiting-for-jwks hook. tagging devon + ashley for review.

support-bot: Notifying customers that requested SLA credits will be handled per incident process. Logging affected API keys for follow-up.

ashley.k: handing off to devon for longer monitoring window. If we hit >1% 401 rate again, re-open incident.

oncall-handoff: oncall-handoff: next oncall is devon, handoff at 15:22 UTC.

devon: acknowledged handoff. I'll keep a 60-minute watch and follow up with postmortem doc. adding action items to incident board.

incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated) — Root cause: premature key rollout without JWKS propagation guard. Severity downgraded. Postmortem owner: devon.

ashley.k: thanks team. please add any follow-ups to the postmortem and link to the deploy pipeline PR. :thumbsup:
